newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica wants U.S. help to capture serial killer.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica wants U.S. help to capture serial killer.

text.p: Costa Rica has asked the FBI for help in tracking down a serial killer who preys on young couples as they make love and has claimed up to 31 victims, often mutilating their bodies.

Costa Rican police said on Friday they hoped the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation could help to identify a man known as "the psychopath" for the grisly string of murders he has carried out over the past decade. They have sometimes included necrophilia.

"The psychopath" preys on young couples in secluded parks in and around the capital San Jose, police said. He often waits until the couples start making love before shooting them with a high-calibre weapon and mutilating their bodies.

"Two police agents and a translator flew to the United States on Thursday to coordinate with U.S. police," said Francisco Ruiz, a spokesman for the Justice Investigation Unit, Costa Rica's version of the FBI.
"We want to solve this case this year," he said, adding that police had asked for several FBI agents to travel to Costa Rica to help crack the case.

Most of the killer's victims have been in a wooded area stretching from the southwestern district of Alajuelita to the eastern neighbourhood of Cartago -- a patch of land that frightened residents now call the "triangle of death."

Costa Rican police have drawn up several psychological profiles of the killer, including one "Rambo" theory that he is a deranged former military or police official. Police said he could also be the son of wealthy politicians or landowners and was believed to be highly intelligent.
The gruesome murders began more than a decade ago, and have stumped Costa Rican police, who are under increasing pressure to solve the case in the face of growing public fear about the serial killer.

Police believe the killer, who is probably in his 30s or 40s, has killed at least 19 people, but they increasingly think he may also be responsible for the disappearance of 12 other young people in the area during 1996.
"We don't know for sure whether the 12 others were his victims, but we can't discount that at all," Ruiz said.

His latest victims were believed to be a 24-year old man and his 23-year-old girlfriend, who were killed on the night of October 26, 1996 with a .45 calibre gun or sub-machine gun as they made love in a San Jose park. The woman was also mutilated, police said.
Police said the killer probably follows his potential victims for several days before killing them. In some cases, he has also been known to kill young women on their own and carry out necrophilia.

Rafael Guillen, a former director of Costa Rica's Justice Investigation Unit, who has followed the case for years, said he believed the killer was carrying out the crimes in revenge for something that happened to him in his youth.
